No email found through any verified channel. Recorded as null.
address_source: Nextdoor business page (nextdoor.com/pages/julians-mobile-detailing-cape-coral-fl/), consistent with prior discovery.
about: Julian Curbelo, 18 years old with about 3 years of detailing experience, runs a mobile detailing operation serving Cape Coral and Fort Myers, FL. He sold his own sedan to invest in a truck rig equipped with its own water and electric hookup, so the whole service happens at the customer's home or office. Nextdoor's community summary describes him as punctual, honest, professional and hardworking, with a business neighbors say is set to 'take Cape Coral by storm.' Named a Nextdoor Neighborhood Favorite in 2024.
instagram_note: Handle confirmed via multiple independent web search results and cited directly in the business's own PocketSuite bio text ('View my work on instagram @juliansmobiledetailing_'). Official web_profile_info API and public IG mirrors (imginn, picnob, pixwox) all blocked; could not pull feed photos or bio directly from Instagram, per pipeline max-2-attempts rule moved to other sources (Nextdoor business gallery/post photos, PocketSuite og:image).
facebook_note: facebook.com/p/Julians-Mobile-Detailing-61560246950705 is the URL most consistently surfaced by search engines under this business name, but a direct fetch of its page content returned an Intro of 'Fairhaven MA' and phone '508-525-1962', which does NOT match this business (Cape Coral FL, phone 239-284-7709). 'Julian's Mobile Detailing' / 'Julian's Mobile Detail' / 'Julian's Mobile Car Expert' are used by at least 4 unrelated businesses found during research (Cape Coral FL - this one, Tampa Bay/St. Pete FL, Fairhaven MA, Hull MA, San Antonio TX): treated as a name collision. reviews_note: Only 2 named, attributable verbatim quotes were found. Yelp (yelp.com/biz/julians-mobile-detailing-cape-coral, lists 24 photos) returned HTTP 403 / CAPTCHA on every fetch attempt (direct curl, WebFetch, and an r.jina.ai proxy fetch), so its reviews could not be pulled. Nextdoor's own AI-generated community summary paragraph (unattributed, not a verbatim named quote) was used only as background copy in the About section, not presented as a review card, per pipeline verbatim-quote rule.
language_source: All source text (Nextdoor bio and reviews, PocketSuite bio, business hashtags) is in English. Cape Coral/Fort Myers FL is an English-language market; no evidence of Spanish-language content or 'se habla espanol' messaging found.
rating_source: Business itself states 'He has 41 5-star reviews on Google' consistently across its Nextdoor business bio summary and multiple independent web search snippets (matches the figure supplied at task start). Could not independently re-pull the live Google Business Profile page directly (Google Maps/Search results pages did not expose lh3.googleusercontent.com or ratings data to a non-JS fetch in this session), so this is the best-available, multiply-corroborated figure, not a fresh first-party pull. Secondary data point: PocketSuite's own in-platform review widget separately shows 4.8 stars / 62 reviews (a different, PocketSuite-specific review pool) -- not used as the headline stat since the Google figure is the one directly volunteered by the business and echoed everywhere it's mentioned.

selected.origin: Nextdoor business logo / matches PocketSuite og:image family

discarded: Business logo graphic was NOT used as a large gallery tile (only as small circular avatar/favicon) to avoid a blown-up low-res vector-style image in the photo gallery.

A Jeep Wrangler interior shot with plastic seat/wheel protective covers and a visible promo business-card overlay was excluded from the gallery (protective covering + on-image text reads as in-progress/promotional rather than a clean finished-result shot).

Several near-duplicate crops of the same vehicles (multiple angles of the same Corvette, same Jeep, same blue-camo truck) were downloaded but only the strongest angle of each vehicle was kept to avoid a repetitive gallery.
images.curation_note: 10 real, verified photos used (9 vehicle/detail photos + 1 logo), well above the 6-14 target. All visually inspected: no selfies, no closed-eyes/mid-procedure shots, no text-overlay screenshots. Strong variety across trucks, Jeeps, and exotic cars (Ferrari, Audi R8, Corvette), which reads as authentic proof of real client work rather than stock imagery.

brand_vibe: Julian's own logo is red, chrome/silver and black: a spray-gun and car silhouette graphic on a black shield with 'EXCELLENT DETAIL SERVICE'. The real photo set (mobile rig, exotic and lifted-truck clientele in Cape Coral driveways) reads as youth-led, energetic and premium-adjacent without being a luxury storefront. Dark base with a vivid racing-red accent and a chrome/steel secondary tone (used in the footer/CTA band) mirrors the logo's own red+chrome+black identity directly, rather than reusing an unrelated color story.

build_notes: Dark template (templates/dark-v2, ejemplar Pure Artistry) derived via anchored transformation script (python, asserts on every rep()). Palette shifted from gold to a racing-red + graphite/chrome scheme (badge protected/untouched, stays gold per DESIGN.md). Bilingual EN(default)/ES implemented, toggle in nav. 'El Metodo' 4-step section rewritten into the real detailing workflow: book online, mobile setup arrival (own water/electric), wash/decon/correct, protect & finish. Services section adapted to quote-based cards (no invented prices) following the oddjobrob precedent. Reviews section reduced from 3 to 2 cards (grid adjusted to 2 columns) since only 2 named verbatim quotes were verifiable (Yelp blocked). JSON-LD type AutoDetailing with makesOffer (no price field, since none verified). Gate passed clean (0 em-dash, all markers present, no leftover strings from the Pure Artistry skeleton, JSON-LD valid, applyLang default = en matches <html lang="en">).
